Introduce support for representing pointers to objects allocated by the
BPF program
column2: i.e. PTR_TO_BTF_ID that point to a type in program BTF.

column1: This is indicated by the presence of MEM_ALLOC type flag in reg->type to
avoid having to check btf_is_kernel when trying to match argument types
in helpers.
Whenever walking such types
column2: any pointers being walked will always yield

column1: a SCALAR instead of pointer. In the future we might permit kptr inside
such allocated objects (either kernel or program allocated)
then form a PTR_TO_BTF_ID of the respective type.
For now
column2: such allocated objects will always be referenced in verifier

column1: context
column2: hence ref_obj_id == 0 for them is a bug. It is allowed to write

column1: to such objects
column2: as long fields that are special are not touched

column1: (support for which will be added in subsequent patches). Note that once
such a pointer is marked PTR_UNTRUSTED
column2: it is no longer allowed to write

column1: to it.
No PROBE_MEM handling is therefore done for loads into this type unless
PTR_UNTRUSTED is part of the register type
column2: since they can never be in

column1: an undefined state
column2: and their lifetime will always be valid.
